topic: Necessary-and-sufficient DOG-invariant total-effect certification under simultaneous latent confounding and measurement error. In Yang et al.'s canonical separable, minimal, rank-faithful linear LV-SEM-ME with known observation labels, characterize the complete pairwise total-effect image over every minimum-edge DOG model; prove the normalized-column projection, singleton minor iff, attaining countermodels, polynomial global minimum-completion algorithm, and confidence-region inference. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: exact reductions, witnesses, destructive checks, and all remaining gaps are recorded in <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/eid_lvsemme_dog_effect_certificate.md. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: polynomial constrained minimum completion under coupled downstream cancellations. EARLY KILL TEST: recover and certify the recorded faithful 12-edge plateau optimum.

open_problems.open_problem: For every ordered pair of labeled substantive variables in a canonical separable, minimal, LV-SEM-ME-faithful model, characterize the complete total-effect image over all minimum-edge DOG representatives and give a necessary-and-sufficient normalized-column minor criterion for when that image is a singleton.

source_refs.claim: Yang et al. identify LV-SEM-ME models only up to DOG equivalence and establish effect robustness for a four-node union model, but do not characterize every pairwise total-effect image over the DOG class.
source_refs.author: Yuqin Yang, Mohamed Nafea, Negar Kiyavash, Kun Zhang, AmirEmad Ghassami

source_refs.claim: For latent-variable LiNGAM without measurement error, the paper identifies the set of observationally compatible causal effects and gives structural conditions for singleton identification.
source_refs.author: Saber Salehkaleybar, AmirEmad Ghassami, Negar Kiyavash, Kun Zhang

source_refs.claim: The paper gives complete graphical criteria for identifiable direct and total effects in latent-confounder LiNGAM, but does not cover simultaneous measurement error or DOG equivalence.
source_refs.author: Daniele Tramontano, Yaroslav Kivva, Saber Salehkaleybar, Mathias Drton, Negar Kiyavash

open_problems.why_unsolved: Yang et al.'s load-bearing object is the model equivalence class, not the image of a fixed pairwise total-effect functional on that class; its effect analysis treats a special four-node union construction rather than all labeled pairs. Salehkaleybar et al. and Tramontano et al. characterize effect ambiguity under latent-confounder LiNGAM, but their admissible transformations do not include the center/noise reassignment and measurement-label constraints of LV-SEM-ME. The missing step is to propagate a DOG center swap through normalized mixing columns and prove that the resulting rational effect differences vanish exactly when the relevant minors vanish; necessity also requires faithful minimum-edge representatives attaining the non-singleton values.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem expressing each pairwise effect set as an explicit image of normalized columns of the recovered mixing matrix, proving a minor-based iff singleton criterion, and giving faithful minimum-edge countermodels that attain every listed alternative value.

writing_exemplar.why: Its narrative starts from simultaneous latent confounding and measurement error, introduces DOG equivalence as the recoverable object, and motivates causal-effect robustness beyond special designs.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: latent confounding and measurement error jointly defeat ordinary discovery -> separability and faithfulness recover only a DOG class -> applications need to know which total effects, rather than merely which models, are invariant across that class

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze admissible mixing-matrix column swaps, derive how each swap changes a total-effect entry through path polynomials, and prove necessity using an explicit swapped model.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired DOG certificate likewise asks whether a specified total-effect coordinate is invariant under a restricted family of observationally invisible column and center reassignments.

method_exemplars.technique: Enumerate observationally compatible latent-variable LiNGAM parameterizations and project them onto the causal-effect coordinate, with graphical conditions collapsing the image to one value.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the closest precedent for treating a causal-effect image, rather than full structure recovery, as the primary identified object.

method_exemplars.technique: Repeatedly perturb discovery statistics, screen admissible graphs, and union graph-specific effect intervals to obtain asymptotic coverage of a fixed causal effect.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once the DOG image is characterized, its sample analogue is also a union over discrete compatible models, so screened union intervals provide a direct inference template.

open_problems.open_problem: Given a recovered mixing matrix and its DOG groups, can the globally minimum-edge center/noise assignment and induced pairwise total-effect image be computed in polynomial time without Cartesian enumeration, even when downstream coefficient cancellations couple choices across groups?

source_refs.claim: The published recovery algorithm enumerates center and noise choices with a multiplicative choice factor that can grow exponentially in the number of groups.
source_refs.author: Yuqin Yang, Mohamed Nafea, Negar Kiyavash, Kun Zhang, AmirEmad Ghassami

source_refs.claim: For a different non-Gaussian latent-confounding model, the paper turns a necessary-and-sufficient parameter-identification criterion into an algorithm polynomial in the number of observed variables.
source_refs.author: Daniele Tramontano, Mathias Drton, Jalal Etesami

source_refs.claim: Markov-equivalent DAGs can be enumerated with linear delay using local transformations, but this machinery does not address DOG center/noise assignments or a global minimum-edge objective.
source_refs.author: Marcel Wienöbst, Malte Luttermann, Max Bannach, Maciej Liśkiewicz

open_problems.why_unsolved: Yang et al. establish that DOG members are precisely the minimum-edge members of the broader AOG class, but their recovery procedure finds the minimum by enumerating center and noise assignments. Adjacent algorithmic literature supplies polynomial identifiability tests or output-sensitive enumeration only for different equivalence structures. The first proof step that must change is the Cartesian loop over row and column assignments: it must be replaced by a decomposable optimization invariant or dynamic program. This is nontrivial because choosing a center changes inverse-matrix coefficients downstream, so zero and nonzero edges can arise through cancellations involving several earlier choices rather than an additive per-group cost; the literature scan found no result occupying this DOG-specific constrained minimum-completion problem.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either a polynomial-time algorithm with a correctness proof and explicit runtime for global minimum-edge DOG completion and effect-image projection, or a regime-specific hardness theorem paired with a polynomial algorithm under sharply stated additional structure.

writing_exemplar.why: Its identification-to-recovery progression and explicit combinatorial choice factor make the computational bottleneck concrete without changing the model.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: DOG equivalence is the sharp population identification object -> current recovery enumerates center and noise assignments -> scalable effect certification requires optimizing the minimum completion without materializing the class

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce generic parameter identifiability to a graphical criterion and prove a polynomial implementation by replacing continuous parameter ambiguity with finite combinatorial tests.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It demonstrates that an ICA-induced latent-variable ambiguity that appears algebraic can sometimes be collapsed to a polynomial certificate, exactly the intended destination for DOG completion.

method_exemplars.technique: Use local equivalence-preserving transformations and amortized analysis to traverse a graph-equivalence class with linear delay and bounded structural change between outputs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A local DOG center-swap calculus with controlled updates is a plausible route to avoid recomputing each completion from scratch, although the global-cancellation constraint remains to be resolved.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct confidence regions for the full pairwise DOG total-effect image from i.i.d. observations that account jointly for mixing-matrix estimation, rank and support decisions, minimum-edge model selection, and non-singleton effect ambiguity.

source_refs.claim: The finite-sample study uses an oracle regression on simulated latent sources, describes it as not practically available, and identifies accurate mixing-matrix estimation as a bottleneck.
source_refs.author: Yuqin Yang, Mohamed Nafea, Negar Kiyavash, Kun Zhang, AmirEmad Ghassami

source_refs.claim: Bellot derives causal-effect bounds over a PAG equivalence class but states that the reported bounds do not account for uncertainty in graph discovery or bound approximation.
source_refs.author: Alexis Bellot

source_refs.claim: The paper obtains asymptotically correct coverage for a fixed causal effect after constraint-based DAG or CPDAG discovery using a resampling, screening, and union construction.
source_refs.author: Ting-Hsuan Chang, Zijian Guo, Daniel Malinsky

open_problems.why_unsolved: Yang et al.'s population theory assumes that the mixing matrix is available up to permutation and scale; its finite-sample study supplies perturbations of the true matrix or an oracle regression using latent sources, then thresholds supports and coefficients without coverage guarantees. Existing post-discovery inference treats DAG or CPDAG selection driven by conditional-independence or score statistics, while equivalence-class effect methods assume a PAG or CPDAG functional rather than an overcomplete-ICA matrix followed by discontinuous rank, support, center, and sparsity decisions. A valid region must propagate first-stage ICA uncertainty through a set-valued, nonregular projection and remain honest near tied completions and nearly vanishing minors.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An implementable estimator of the DOG effect set together with a theorem giving asymptotically honest simultaneous coverage and either Hausdorff convergence or a local-limit characterization under explicit separation margins.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames accurate first-stage mixing recovery as a practical bottleneck and cleanly separates population DOG recovery from noisy finite-sample inputs.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: population separability reveals a mixing matrix -> DOG recovery maps that matrix to an equivalence class and effect claims -> real data provide only a noisy ICA estimate, so uncertainty must cover both discrete model ambiguity and continuous effect estimation

method_exemplars.technique: Randomly perturb discovery statistics, retain screened graph candidates, and form a union of graph-specific intervals whose proof controls exclusion of the true graph and conditional interval error.
method_exemplars.why_closest: DOG inference also requires a confidence object robust to discrete discovery mistakes while targeting a fixed population causal effect rather than a selected functional.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive a measurement-error-corrected method-of-moments statistic, variance-stabilize it, and prove asymptotic normality and consistency of the induced causal-discovery procedure.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides model-specific precedent for propagating measurement-error moments into calibrated rank and conditional-independence decisions rather than treating the corrected population matrix as known.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive an influence function from an equivalence-class identification algorithm and cross-fit a double or debiased estimator to obtain end-to-end effect estimation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired procedure similarly begins with an equivalence-class identifying map and needs a principled route from that map to an estimator and limit law.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the sharp separation margin under which a singleton DOG total-effect certificate is stable to perturbations of the recovered mixing matrix, and characterize the local impossibility or set-valued limit when a decisive rank minor approaches zero.

source_refs.claim: LV-SEM-ME faithfulness excludes exact cancellations only on measure-zero sets, while the numerical recovery study uses fixed thresholds and reports sensitivity to noisy mixing matrices.
source_refs.author: Yuqin Yang, Mohamed Nafea, Negar Kiyavash, Kun Zhang, AmirEmad Ghassami

source_refs.claim: Ordinary faithfulness is insufficient for uniform causal inference with unknown order or latent confounding, motivating explicit quantitative separation conditions.
source_refs.author: James M. Robins, Richard Scheines, Peter Spirtes, Larry Wasserman

source_refs.claim: The paper formulates strengthened faithfulness conditions under which causal procedures can be uniformly consistent and treats ordinary faithfulness as a limiting case.
source_refs.author: Jiji Zhang, Peter L. Spirtes

open_problems.why_unsolved: Generic DOG identifiability distinguishes exact zero from nonzero minors but supplies no quantitative radius within which the effect certificate is invariant. A faithful sequence may approach the algebraic cancellation variety arbitrarily closely, making support, rank, and minimum-edge choices discontinuous. Uniform-consistency theory explains why a qualitative measure-zero exclusion is inadequate, but its strong-faithfulness margins concern conditional independences in DAG or PAG discovery, not normalized mixing-column minors and coupled completion scores in LV-SEM-ME. The first missing argument is a perturbation bound linking singular values or decisive minors of the normalized mixing matrix to preservation of every admissible completion and its effect image.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient quantitative margin theorem for local constancy of the singleton effect certificate, paired with contiguous countermodels or a minimax lower bound showing failure of uniform certification as that margin vanishes.

writing_exemplar.why: Its population genericity assumptions and threshold-based perturbation experiment naturally motivate replacing qualitative faithfulness with an operational margin.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: DOG identification holds away from algebraic cancellation sets -> finite samples perturb every rank and support quantity -> useful certification requires the exact distance-to-boundary condition governing stability

method_exemplars.technique: Construct nearby causal models to prove non-uniformity under qualitative faithfulness and identify quantitative restrictions that restore uniformly reliable inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The DOG minor-zero variety creates the same local-alternative mechanism: observational laws can be arbitrarily close while their valid singleton-effect conclusions differ.

method_exemplars.technique: Replace qualitative faithfulness with parameterized lower bounds on detectable associations and prove uniform consistency under the resulting margin class.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The corresponding transfer is to lower-bound the singular values or normalized-column minors that decide DOG membership and effect invariance.

method_exemplars.technique: Use resampling and screening to retain multiple plausible equivalence-class models and union their intervals when selection is unstable.
method_exemplars.why_closest: At small DOG margins, honest inference should widen from a singleton interval to a union over locally plausible effect values instead of forcing a discontinuous point certificate.

literature_map:
Yang et al. (2026, IJAR; arXiv:2407.19426) is the direct anchor: separability, minimality, and LV-SEM-ME faithfulness identify a canonical simultaneous-confounding and measurement-error model only up to DOG equivalence.
Yang et al. (2022, NeurIPS; arXiv:2211.03984) introduced AOG and DOG machinery for the two challenges separately and tied recovery to mixing-matrix sparsity.
Zhang et al. (2018, UAI) study structural identifiability under measurement error but do not characterize the full effect image when uniqueness fails.
Hoyer et al. (2010, IJAR; DOI 10.1016/j.ijar.2008.02.006) use overcomplete ICA for causal-effect estimation with hidden variables and motivate canonical latent-root reductions.
Salehkaleybar et al. (2020, JMLR; arXiv:1908.03932) make the set of compatible causal effects explicit for latent-variable LiNGAM, supplying the closest effect-image precedent.
Tramontano et al. (2024, ICML; arXiv:2406.02049) give complete swap-based graphical criteria for direct and total-effect identifiability under latent confounding, but not simultaneous measurement error.
Tramontano, Drton, and Etesami (2026, Annals of Statistics; DOI 10.1214/25-AOS2597) show that another latent-confounding parameter-identification problem admits a polynomial graphical certificate.
Wang and Drton (2023, JMLR; arXiv:2007.11131) obtain exact structure recovery for bow-free non-Gaussian mixed graphs, illustrating how stronger structural restrictions collapse equivalence.
Maathuis, Kalisch, and Bühlmann (2009, Annals of Statistics; DOI 10.1214/09-AOS685) introduced IDA's local computation of a multiset of total effects over a CPDAG rather than enumerating every DAG.
Bellot (2024, UAI; arXiv:2311.07259) derives analytical effect bounds from PAG invariants but notes that graph and bound-estimation uncertainty remains unaddressed and relevant-graph enumeration is costly.
Jung, Tian, and Bareinboim (2021, ICML; PMLR 139) derive influence functions and DML estimators for effects identifiable from a PAG, providing an inference analogue once an equivalence-class functional is known.
Saeed et al. (2020, UAI; arXiv:1906.00928) prove asymptotically normal measurement-error-corrected tests and consistent graph recovery, but in an anchored Gaussian model without simultaneous latent confounding.
Chang, Guo, and Malinsky (2026, Biometrika; DOI 10.1093/biomet/asaf073) and Gradu et al. (2025, JASA; DOI 10.1080/01621459.2024.2402089) address post-discovery coverage for DAG or CPDAG procedures, not ICA-driven DOG selection.
Wienöbst et al. (2023, AAAI; DOI 10.1609/aaai.v37i10.26451) provide linear-delay MEC enumeration; Yang's DOG recovery instead retains a combinatorial center and noise-choice factor with no polynomial global minimum-completion theorem.
Robins et al. (2003, Biometrika; DOI 10.1093/biomet/90.3.491) and Zhang and Spirtes (2012; arXiv:1212.2506) expose the tension between generic faithfulness and uniform reliability, which reappears near zero DOG rank minors.
